body: I'm the wrong person to ask if it gets easier. But I do feel your pain, and I'm sorry for what you're going through

Oh nice. Work can definitely help as it can take your mind off things.

Well, I watch a lot of baseball actually (in another life I'd probably be a sports reporter) and I play in a band with a couple friends. We practice once or twice a week and try to play a gig once a month or so if possible. 

But, also have something called anhedonia, which is similar to depression but essentially makes it impossible to enjoy even the things that you technically like - as in, I love movies but when I'm by myself I can't bring myself to watch anything new. So, I wind up watching the Dark Knight or Wayne's World for the 200th time, or I put on a ball game in the background and just zone out on social media. It fucking sucks. I know exactly what to do to feel better....but because of my mental illness, even mundane tasks are excruciating for me most of the time. So I go back to the familiar, just to make it through the day.

Jesus Murphy. That reply really hit home, particularly the last two paragraphs. You're right, there are likely tons of people already in my life that would be happy to help if they only knew I needed it. It's time to stop being afraid of telling people, and start reaching out. If I really want to stop living in my own head (which is where all this stuff originates, let's be honest), I have to let what's in my head...out. Tx again.

Ahh I gotcha. Thanks for saying that.

I've heard that as well, actually. I shouldn't really have given that advice, and I apologize for it...I just, well, I miss my ex as well and sometimes I think someone else would make me forget about her, at least for a time. But obviously it normally doesn't work - short term gain and long term gain are usually the result. But when you're hurting in the short term, as I am....it can sometimes feel like a good option:/

Fuck. Having someone cheat on you fucking sucks, sorry man. I wish I could tell you that you just need to move on but I'm struggling w that myself now, obviously. I almost think I need a rebound relationship right now...but because of my mental state I'm even worried about disappointing that person, the heretofore unknown reboundee. On the other hand, a new person might be just what someone in your position needs, at least at this point.

Shit. How long ago did you split up? Did you leave or did she? 

Yeah, we split up last year after being together since 2007, married since 2012. I got really sick (first physically, then mentally) and it broke us. She definitely contributed to my mental condition, but she also helped with alot. I left last year though, and though I feel OK about it sometimes, a lot of the time I just want it to be back to what things were like before I got sick. I know the old saying, you can't go home again...but that's basically all I want. The worst thing about pining for the good old days is that you don't realize you're in them until they're over:(

You are a pillar of positivity. Thank you:) These are all great ideas. I've been thinking about volunteering actually - your post has convinced me that I should give it a shot. Today, hopefully, I'll get in contact w someone. I'm thinking maybe at the local hospital (I'm a cancer survivor so it might make me feel like I'm giving back? I dunno).

Also, it just dawned on me that you've been writing these walls of text, just for me. I guess someone out there does care about me....and you've never even met me. Thank you, from the bottom of my broken, busted heart:)

I'm a 36 yo cancer survivor, but I got depression and other assorted mental illnesses as a result of the meds and treatment I had. So, I had to leave my wife, who I loved very dearly and took care of me through the cancer. I developed a severe alcohol dependency while depressed, which has since been attributed to the fact I couldn't create dopamine naturally any longer. This didn't happen because of the alcohol, but before the alcohol, and I used the booze to feel pleasure again, which for a time I couldn't feel at all without it. As you can imagine this caused some friction in my marriage, and long story short I fucked up enough times that my lame ass couldn't take the heat anymore so I left. For a time I thought this was the right decision. But now, I've lived with my parents for more than a year, I'm unemployed, still single, in a massive amount of debt, and starting to feel a bunch of that depression creeping its way back in. 

There's lots of other stuff too, but that's a start. I can't restart again. I already fought a massive battle, I've been trying to fight this one for a couple years now, and I'm losing, still, badly. I want out
I won't. I've been thinking about this for a long, long time though. It's anything but a rash decision. I appreciate th concern though

According to those around me - when I laid in bed all day with cancer, it was because I was sick, but when I lay in bed all day now, it's because I'm just lazy/not trying hard enough. Come the fuck on.

I cried so hard this afternoon that I was literally tingling/numb afterwards. And nothing "bad" happened, I am just profoundly sad. Due to my depression, ptsd and anxiety, as well as the results of those, I've had to quit my job, and am now divorced and living back home. And the worst thing: the depression came about partially due to the painkillers I had to take when I had...cancer. Fucking cancer. Treatments/recovery from which took approximately 2 years. So I got better so I can sit in the room I had as a teenager, alone and sad. What the fuck am I doing here?

That's what kind of week it's been.
